gap.title: Open, a hard one: can a long deterministic computation always be checked faster by three rounds of guessing? It may be false
gap.statement: ∃ p q : ℕ, 1 ≤ p ∧ p < q ∧ PEqualNP.Library.FP3 p q
gap.unlocks: With the checked L-lib-122 it gives a separation: nondeterministic linear time is not inside deterministic time n^c for some c above 1, on our machines. It is the one open link of a chain that is otherwise checked
gap.context: OPEN: A HARD ONE. It may be false. Any saving in the exponent, however small, is enough. It fails relative to some oracles, so a proof must use the content of the computation. No mechanism is known here after three rounds of attempts; the dead ones, with reasons, are in routes/evasion/DEAD-ENDS.md. A proof must prove exactly the recorded statement, with no sorry, no new axiom and no native_decide. Put every declaration of your file inside its own namespace.
dead: trading alternations for savings: the known saving is tiny and already available at two alternations
compressible configurations: fails relative to a random oracle
